newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's Rostamani takes 20 pct of Jumbo Electronics.
newsitem.headline: UAE's Rostamani takes 20 pct of Jumbo Electronics.

text.p: Dubai family conglomerate Rostamani Group has taken a 20 percent stake in leading Middle East electronics distributor Jumbo Electronics Co Ltd, the companies said on Tuesday.
At a news briefing, Jumbo Group chairman Manohar Chhabria and Rostamani chairman Abdullah Hassan al-Rostamani said the agreement was signed on December 15.

Neither would give the value of the stake, but in June Jumbo said it hoped to sell the 15,000 shares, with a nominal value of 1,000 dirhams each, at 6,000 dirhams each, raising 90 million dirhams ($25 million).

Rostamani said Jumbo's capital would be doubled to 150 million dirhams within the next month. It was not clear how much of this the Rostamani Group would put up, in addition to its 20 percent share of the current 75 million dirham capital.

Jumbo, with annual turnover of 1.4 billion dirhams and 75,000 authorised shares, was previously 51 percent owned by a United Arab Emirates family and 49 percent by Indian businessman Chhabria. Rostamani, with annual turnover of 4.4 billion dirhams, bought the 20 percent from the family.
With its new partner, Jumbo -- which distributes mainly Sony and its own brand, Supra, products -- said it planned to step up investment in marketing and distribution in the Gulf.

It also planned to spend 125 million dirhams on a plant in Dubai to manufacture 200,000 Supra refrigerators annually. The factory will also produce 20,000 freezers, 30,000 ovens and 15,000 "ice cream conservers" a year, Jumbo said. ($1=3.67 dirhams)
